stories.headline: SECONDARY PICKET UPHELD BY COURT; U. S. Appeals Bench Permits Boycott of Consumers and of Farmed-Out Work
stories.summary: US Appeals Ct rules union may picket consumers using services provided by a struck employer and ind cos doing 'farmed-out' struck work of employer, Royal Typewriter case; definition of secondary boycott under Taft-Hartley law seen revised

stories.summary: Wagner, Jack rept Title I middle-income project planned, Whitehall, Water and South Sts and Coenties Slip; illus; sketch; map

stories.headline: 15-CENT BUS FARE ON PRIVATE LINES APPROVED BY CITY; Increases for 8 Companies Attacked by Klein at a 6-Hour Public Hearing COUNCIL PAY IS RAISED Sharkey and Isaacs Receive Salary Advances, Others $2,000 More for Costs 15-Cent Fare, Effective Sunday, Approved on 8 Private Bus Lines
stories.summary: The Board of Estimate unanimously approved yesterday a 15-cent fare on the eight privately operated bus lines in Manhattan, Queens and the Bronx.

stories.headline: U. S. ASKS PRIORITY FOR AERIAL CHECK IN U. N. ARMS TALKS; Western Resolution Proposes Assembly Stress Program Offered by Eisenhower 5-POWER PARLEY URGED American Exhibit Employed to Show the Practicability of Inspection by Planes U. S. Asks the U. N. Give Priority To Eisenhower Idea in Arms Talk
stories.summary: US, GB, France, Canada ask Assembly recommend priority for Eisenhower plan in future discussions, resolution to com; ask subcom talks resume; urge instituting steps such as Eisenhower, Bulganin plans pending gen accord; urge study of Eden, Faure plans; Nutting presents resolution; chides Kuznetsov for making much of USSR relinquishing some bases; asks more evidence of good faith; US opens exhibit, NYC, to show feasibility of aerial inspection; illus; Lodge guides UN diplomats including Sobolev; says US or USSR could be completely surveyed in 6 mos

stories.headline: ASTRONAUTS SPEEDING TOWARD THE MOON; FIRST DAY OF APOLLO FLIGHT IS FLAWLESS; NIXON ASKS FOR NATIONAL HOLIDAY MONDAY; CRAFT ON TARGET World Watches Start of Man's Attempt to Achieve Landing Astronauts Speeding Toward the Moon; First Day of Apollo 11 Flight Is Flawless World Watches the Start Of Attempt for a Landing
stories.summary: CAPE KENNEDY, Fla., Thursday, -- Three American astronauts commissioned to fulfill an age-old dream and a national goal of the decade were streaking across the black sea of space today in man's first attempt to walk on another world -- the moon.

stories.headline: NIXON PLANS CUT IN MILITARY ROLE FOR U.S. IN ASIA; Starting Tour, He Promises Respect for Commitments, but Under New Forms ARRIVES IN PHILIPPINES President, at Guam, Asserts Nation Won't Be Drawn Into More Vietnams President Nixon Declares That U.S. Will Reduce Its Military Commitments in Asia POLICIES OUTLINED AT START OF TOUR He Says Nation Will Not Be Drawn Into Future Wars Like That in Vietnam
stories.summary: Nixon says he may order reduction in mil operations in S Vietnam if it would help negotiations to end war, news conf, Guam; favors summit meeting with USSR in search for end of war, but doubts USSR would work for settlement in pub forum; concedes many Amers are frustrated with war and want reduction in US commitment

stories.headline: HOUSE UNIT ACTS TO INCREASE TAX ON CAPITAL GAINS; Mills Also Indicates Action by Committee to Reduce Oil-Depletion Allowance SENATE DEBATE GOES ON Long and Dirksen Continue to Press for Early Move on Surcharge Extension House Unit Acting on Capital Gains
stories.summary: Maneuvering continues in Sen on linking tax reform and income tax surcharge extension; Sen E M Kennedy hacks view of Dem leadership that entire matter should be treated jointly in Sept; offers 8 major reforms

stories.headline: BURGER TO PRESS JUDICIAL REFORM; Pledges to Make Off-Bench Effort in Drive to Improve Administration of Justice BURGER TO PRESS JUDICIAL REFORM
stories.summary: Chief Justice Burger disputes Time magazine statement that he is concerned that recent Sup Ct decisions have hampered criminal prosecutors, int; says he backs stronger defense side

stories.headline: ALLIES CONFRONT BAGHDAD DEFENDERS; IRAQIS REPEL COPTERS; ONE GOES DOWN
stories.summary: American forces gather south of Baghdad, flinging artillery fire and attack helicopters against Republican Guard, outer ring of Saddam Hussein's defense of Baghdad; curtain of fire from small arms and machine guns drives back airborne force of 32 Apache helicopters seeking Iraqi tanks; nearly all helicopters sustain damage, and one goes down in farmer's field; its two crewmen are listed as missing in action; Iraqi state television runs video of two captured men; allied forces regroup to consider shift in strategy to take on Medina Republican Guard Division's armor from safer altitudes; heavy aerial bombardment is unleashed on targets south of Baghdad; Iraq appears to be pursuing military strategy of concentrating its forces in cities, where they are less immediately vulnerable to superior allied firepower; Deputy Prime Min Tariq Aziz appears buoyant during televised news conference while describing results of day's battles; photos; map (M)

stories.headline: 'Chicago' Is Big Oscar Winner, but 'Pianist' Surprises; Hollywood Glamour Still Stars at Ceremony, but Security and War Play Supporting Roles
stories.summary: Chicago wins best picture and five other Oscars while losing a few upsets to The Pianist, including Roman Polanski winning award for best director; winners include Nicole Kidman for best actress (The Hours), Adrien Brody for best actor (Pianist), Chris Cooper for best supporting actor (Adaptation) and Catherine Zeta-Jones for best supporting actress (Chicago); war in Iraq dims glamour of ceremonies only slightly, but it is reflected in several acceptance speeches, notably Michael Moore's for his Oscar for best documentary (Bowling for Columbine); Moore attacks Pres Bush as ficticious president leading war on ficticious grounds; comments are booed by many people in audience; photos (L)

stories.headline: Gulf War Witnesses, at an Intimate Level; As a New Conflict Looms, Two Memoirs Examine a Past One
stories.summary: Persian Gulf war of is focus of two new memoirs: Jarhead by Anthony Swofford, who served as Marine sniper on Saudi-Kuwait border, and Baghdad Express by Joel Turnipseed, Marine reservist who ferried truckloads of ammunition and supplies across Saudi desert to American troops on front lines; photos (M)

stories.headline: Untested Companies Enlist in U.S. Biodefense
stories.summary: Efforts in United States to create vibrant biodefense sector have left national security against bioterorism largely in hands of untested companies; about 100 biotechnology companies are trying to develop technology for detecting or fighting pathogens that may be used by terrorists or rogue nations; many are small companies, lured by government research money, that have never brought product to market successfully; Bush administration plan to spend some $6 billion over 10 years to buy and stockpile medicines to counter biological, chemical and radiological weapons will create guaranteed market for drugs; table of possible threats and companies working to counter them; photos (M)

rounds.blurb: Among the month's major headlines: ALLIES CONFRONT BAGHDAD DEFENDERS; 'Chicago' Is Big Oscar Winner, but 'Pianist' Surprises; Gulf War Witnesses, at an Intimate Level.
